neighbours.label: ' (' opening the spelled-out expansion right after an acronym, e.g. 'MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)'
fire: The hospital will arrange a CT (computed tomography) scan of your chest.
Your heart rhythm can be checked with an ECG (electrocardiogram) in a few minutes.
Patients may need a PET (positron emission tomography) scan before surgery.
The study used fMRI (functional magnetic resonance imaging) to watch the brain at work.
Doctors measured her BMI (body mass index) at every visit.
Severe cases may be treated with ECMO (extracorporeal membrane oxygenation) in intensive care.
The nurse took a sample for a CBC (complete blood count) before the operation.
An EEG (electroencephalogram) records the electrical activity of the brain.
quiet: The hospital will arrange a CT scan of your chest next week (if a slot is free).
Your heart rhythm can be checked with an ECG in a few minutes at the clinic.
Patients may need a PET scan before surgery (see the leaflet for details).
The study used fMRI to watch the brain at work during simple tasks.
Doctors measured her BMI at every visit (about once a month).
Severe cases may be treated with ECMO in intensive care for several days.
The nurse took a sample for a CBC before the operation began.
An EEG records the electrical activity of the brain through the scalp.

notes: Probe: 'MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)' 0.97 on ' ('. A non-gloss parenthesis ('(see Figure 2)', '(Ganymede)', '(about 70 percent)') stayed at or below 0.03, and the chemical formula ' Ca' was 0.23. Near misses keep the acronym and either drop the parenthesis or use a non-expansion one.
